skill.name: fiftyone-dataset-import
skill.description: Guides FiftyOne dataset imports for images, videos, point clouds, 3D scenes, labels, and multimodal groups. It scans folders, detects formats, suggests required packages, creates datasets, validates counts, and launches the FiftyOne App.
skill.summary: Import and validate diverse computer vision datasets in FiftyOne.
skill.author: AdonaiVera

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, code fences, examples, or benign FiftyOne references. Confirmed issues are limited to package installation guidance and Python import checks that can execute third-party code. A high-risk semantic issue remains because the skill recommends pickle.load on dataset files.

remediation.issue: Unsafe pickle loading from dataset annotations
remediation.suggestion: Replace pickle examples with safe parsers when possible. If pickle is unavoidable, warn users to load only trusted files in an isolated environment.

remediation.issue: Remote package installation from PyPI and GitHub
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, pin package versions, prefer verified sources, and recommend a dedicated virtual environment.
Quote user-provided paths and prefer Python pathlib examples for portable scanning. Avoid xargs when simple find or Python code is enough.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Check if packages are installed** using `pip show <package>`
| Waymo Open | `waymo-open-dataset-tf` | See Waymo docs (requires TensorFlow) |
| Point cloud conversion to PCD | `open3d` | `pip install open3d` |
- **Rename**: Use a different name (suggest alternatives like `dataset-name-v2`)
| `*.xml` files with Pascal VOC structure | VOC | `VOC` |
| Folder-per-class structure | Classification | `Image Classification Directory Tree` |
- Search PyPI first: `pip search <package>` or check pypi.org
This dataset appears to be in PandaSet format, which requires the `pandaset` package.
3. **Convert point clouds to PCD format** (FiftyOne requires `.pcd` files)
4. **Create `fo.Scene` objects** for 3D visualization with point clouds
Many autonomous driving datasets store LiDAR data in proprietary formats (`.pkl.gz`, `.bin`, `.npy`)
**Note:** Install open3d if needed: `pip install open3d`
For each LiDAR frame, create an `fo.Scene` that references the PCD file:
| CVAT Image | `CVAT Image` | classifications, detections, polylines, keypoints | Single `*.xml` |
| CVAT Video | `CVAT Video` | frame labels | XML directory |
| OpenLABEL Image | `OpenLABEL Image` | all types | `*.json` directory |
| OpenLABEL Video | `OpenLABEL Video` | all types | `*.json` directory |
| TF Object Detection | `TF Object Detection` | detections | TFRecords |
| TF Image Classification | `TF Image Classification` | classification | TFRecords |
| Image Classification Tree | `Image Classification Directory Tree` | classification | Folder per cl
| Video Classification Tree | `Video Classification Directory Tree` | classification | Folder per cl
| Image Segmentation | `Image Segmentation` | segmentation | Mask images |
| FiftyOne Dataset | `FiftyOne Dataset` | all types | Exported format |
- All samples in a group share the same `group.id`
- Each sample has a `group.name` indicating its slice
- Only one `3d` slice allowed per group
git clone https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git && cd <repo> && pip install .
│   └── Format: pickle, Fields: label, position, dimensions, rotation, track_id
4. Use the grid view to see multiple slices side by side
5. **Handle errors gracefully** - Report issues clearly, continue with valid files

content.value_statement: Dataset imports often fail when media, annotations, and multimodal folders use different formats. This skill guides scanning, detection, package setup, import, grouping, and validation in FiftyOne.
actual_capabilities: Scans dataset folders and inventories media, labels, and directory structure.
Maps common formats such as COCO, YOLO, VOC, CVAT, KITTI, and OpenLABEL to FiftyOne settings.
Guides grouped dataset creation for multi-camera, LiDAR, and mixed media workflows.
Identifies required devkit packages and asks before installation.
Validates imported sample counts and opens the FiftyOne App.
Provides Python examples for specialized autonomous driving datasets.
limitations: Requires a running FiftyOne MCP server and Voxel51 plugins.
Specialized formats may require third-party devkit packages.
Custom import examples must be verified against the real dataset schema.
Pickle examples should only be used with trusted files or replaced with safe parsers.

use_cases.title: Import Standard Detection Datasets
use_cases.description: Load image datasets with COCO, YOLO, VOC, CVAT, or KITTI labels into a new FiftyOne dataset.

use_cases.title: Create Multimodal Driving Datasets
use_cases.description: Group camera images, LiDAR point clouds, and labels by scene for autonomous driving review.

use_cases.title: Validate Dataset Migration Results
use_cases.description: Compare imported sample counts, labels, groups, and slices against the source files before analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Import a Simple Image Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner import with known image data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan my image dataset at [path], detect labels, propose a FiftyOne import plan, and wait for my confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Detect Unknown Dataset Format
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate import where the folder format is unclear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [path], identify the media types and annotation format, then recommend the safest FiftyOne import settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create Multimodal Groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [path] for camera, LiDAR, and scene grouping patterns. Propose group slices and a validation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Custom Autonomous Driving Import
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a specialized dataset format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a FiftyOne import plan for [dataset name] at [path], including required packages, conversion steps, and label mapping.

output_examples.input: Import a COCO image dataset from my local folder.
output: Scan summary lists image count, annotation file, and detected COCO structure.
Proposed import settings include dataset name, label field, and source paths.
The assistant asks for confirmation before creating the dataset.

output_examples.input: Load an autonomous driving dataset with cameras and LiDAR.
output: Detected slices include front camera, side cameras, and LiDAR.
Required packages and point cloud conversion steps are listed.
Validation compares expected groups, samples, and label fields.
The response checks paths, supported extensions, label format, and existing dataset names.
It suggests a smaller test import before retrying the full dataset.

best_practices: Scan the folder and present findings before creating a dataset.
Ask for confirmation before installing packages or overwriting datasets.
Validate sample counts, labels, and groups after every import.
anti_patterns: Do not import before confirming detected formats with the user.
Do not flatten multimodal scenes that should stay grouped.
Do not load untrusted pickle files without a safe review process.

faq.question: Does this skill require FiftyOne?
faq.answer: Yes. It assumes FiftyOne, the FiftyOne MCP server, and the listed Voxel51 plugins are available.

faq.question: Can it import YOLO and COCO datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes detection and import guidance for YOLO, COCO, VOC, CVAT, KITTI, and other formats.

faq.question: Can it handle point clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers PCD, PLY, LAS, LAZ, and conversion guidance for other point cloud formats.

faq.question: Will it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: The instructions require user confirmation before installing packages. Review package sources before approving.

faq.question: Can it overwrite existing datasets?
faq.answer: It checks for existing dataset names and asks whether to overwrite, rename, or abort.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted annotation files?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill includes pickle examples, and pickle files can execute code when loaded.
